source: Generated by build-frameworks-page.ps1. Do not edit by hand.

frameworks.title: Not sustainable (short)
frameworks.length: 45-70 seconds (about 150-190 words at a warm pace).
frameworks.job: name a state the viewer is stuck in, agree it can't last, kill the fixes they'd reach for, and show the system that fixes it.
frameworks.awareness: problem aware. They know the state. They haven't found the fix.
frameworks.proof: one volume number and at least one named or specific result.

rows: **Call-out + stuck state + "you know that's not sustainable"**
One sentence. Names who they are and the state they're in, then agrees with what they already feel
"If you're a B2B service company and you're still the main person closing every single deal, you know that's not sustainable."
Credits them for building it, so the next beat isn't an attack
MORPH ad 5: "You built this business to 2 million, 5 million or 10 million a year off of your network, referrals and having a great reputation. But the moment you step out of sales... growth stops."
Two fixes they'd reach for, and why each fails. "Because you know that doesn't work" makes them agree
"The solution isn't to hire more salespeople or delegate sales to everybody else, because you know that doesn't work."
What the system does for them, in their terms, before naming it
"The solution is to build a system where prospects come in already educated and pre-sold... and sales becomes just effectively getting people over the line."
"Just last year, we generated over 135 million pounds in qualified sales pipeline for founders that are taking sales themselves."
MORPH ad 5: "Brooks from Pipeline Formula added $1.8 million in revenue closed... in six months."
What to click, and the qualify step
"If you want to see if you qualify for this, click this ad, answer a few questions about your business, and I'll see you on the other side."

frameworks.title: Renamed problem (short)
frameworks.length: 55-70 seconds (about 160-190 words at a warm pace).
frameworks.job: take the thing the viewer blames, show them it isn't the problem, and give the problem a new name that your mechanism solves.
frameworks.awareness: problem aware with the wrong diagnosis. They think it's their service, their sales skill or their market.
frameworks.proof: one volume number and one named result.

rows: Something they've seen and resent, with no question and no greeting
"You see competitors with worse services than yours getting new clients and growing revenue year over year."
Credit what's good about them, then name what the others have that they don't
"Your service might be better, your clients might be staying longer, you might have a better team, but they are winning in the market because they have an engine..."
Two short sentences: the problem they think they have, then the one they actually have
"You don't have a service problem. You just have a distribution problem."
The named system, and what it does, described through their buyers' pain rather than theirs
"We install an acquisition revenue flywheel... that can directly find and target the right people who are already looking for your solution and are in so much pain..."
One transition line that makes the proof feel earned
"Now, there's only one way to do that."
Volume number, then person + company + figure + timeframe
"$175 million in qualified sales pipeline... Brooks from Pipeline Formula, we added $1.8 million in revenue closed... in six months."
The outcome with a number and a window, then the qualify CTA
"If you want to see how you can add 1 to 3 million to your business in the next 12 months, then click this ad, answer a few questions to see if you even qualify."

frameworks.title: Desire hook (short)
frameworks.length: 35-55 seconds (about 100-150 words at a warm pace).
frameworks.job: open on the outcome the viewer wants, say what delivers it, and prove it fast.
frameworks.awareness: solution aware. They want the result and are weighing ways to get it.
frameworks.proof: one volume number and one or two named results. With no proof, use 04.

rows: "What if every client that you close brought you two to three new clients in the next month?"
Names the mechanism as the answer, then says what it isn't
"That's what a revenue flywheel does. And it's not a campaign or an agency that you have to fund every single month to sustain it."
Who it's built for, with a revenue band
"We install it for B2B service companies that are between 2 and $10 million a year."
One sentence on what the mechanism actually does
"...directly target and find people who are already looking for your solution..."
"Now, there's only one way to do that."
Volume number, then two results in one breath each
"$175 million... Brooks from Pipeline Formula added 1.8 million... Jean Michel added 1.2 million in the same time frame."
Restate the hook's outcome as the reason to click
"So if you want a self-funding acquisition flywheel, then click this ad, answer a few questions to see if you actually qualify."

frameworks.title: STOP-prescription
frameworks.job: stop a fix they're about to try, replay their year back to them, teach three things, then give away a free call.
frameworks.awareness: problem aware and about to act on the wrong fix.
frameworks.proof: none in the lean version. That makes this the right card for a client with thin proof.

rows: "If you think [false fix] is how you get [result], stop. It isn't. Not yet."
"Here's what actually happens in the businesses I talk to." Then present-tense scenes from their year, ending on a metric that doesn't move
"Before you [false fix], you need to understand three things. One... Two... And three..." Each one holds without proof
"Now the good news is, I'll [free diagnosis], for free."
"Because you shouldn't have to pay [someone] thousands of dollars just to find out if [question]."
Says what happens after the click

frameworks.title: Offer-forward with steps
frameworks.length: 60-90 seconds (about 170-240 words at a warm pace).
frameworks.job: lead with the promise, explain the mechanism in three or four plain steps, stack proof, remove the fears, and qualify.
frameworks.awareness: product aware. Best for warm audiences, retargeting, or cold traffic once a promise has been proven in statics.
frameworks.proof: a promise with a number and a window, a named mechanism, and two or three results.

rows: "I'll show you how to [result with number] in the next [window]."
"Thanks to our [named mechanism]. A process we've used to [volume proof]."
"Step one: [plain title]. [What we do], so [what they get]." One or two sentences each. No numbers inside the steps
Two or three, each a sector + figure + timeframe
"And you can do it without [fear 1], [fear 2], or [fear 3]." Exactly three distinct fears
Only if the guarantee has been confirmed in writing
"But it's not for everyone. You need to qualify first. So click this ad, answer a few questions to see if you qualify."

frameworks.title: Agree with the objection ("you're right")
frameworks.length: 90-130 seconds (about 230-330 words at a warm pace).
frameworks.job: say the thing the viewer already believes about why their problem can't be fixed, agree with them, then show why the obvious fixes fail and what works instead.
frameworks.awareness: problem aware, and stuck because of a belief ("nobody can sell like me", "B2B doesn't work on Meta", "I can't trust an agency").
frameworks.proof: light. Joe Milnes uses a credential story, but the card works with one proof line, or none. The explanation does the persuading.

rows: Names who it's for and the state they're in, in their words
"If you're a founder doing the sales in your business and you feel like you're the bottleneck because it all relies on your deep expertise, then this is for you."
**The symptoms, then the belief they hold**
Two or three concrete symptoms, ending on the belief that keeps them stuck

"Every deal needs you on the call. You can't take a week off without the pipeline drying up and you know that you need to hire someone but you can't see how anyone can sell like you can sell without being you."
The agreement. Three words, said straight
Explain it from their side, so the agreement feels earned

"...a salesperson can't sell like you because they're not the founder. They haven't got your knowledge... So a written down version of what you do just won't do it. Neither will you telling them what you do on the calls."
His version is heavy on proof. Skip or shrink for a light-proof script

"I was head of sales enablement at a 50 million pound technology firm where we took graduates... zero to turning over 1 million a month in less than a year... over 300 founders... 185 million pounds in new sales."
**The mechanism, plus a guarantee on the paid work**
One sentence on what gets built, one on the risk reversal
"We'll build you a sales process and training program that gets a salesperson selling as well as you can within eight weeks, or we'll refund you or keep working for free until they do."
**Name the cost of failing, then the free plan**
The money fear in numbers, then the free deliverable, listed
"...dreading the thought of wasting 3K a month on a salesperson who doesn't make it... We'll map out the exact hiring plan... You keep that plan whether or not we choose to work together."
Hands the burden of objecting to the viewer
"So unless you can see a downside that I can't, click the link, book a call, and I'll see you on the other side."

frameworks.title: Displacement, then STOP (25 seconds)
frameworks.length: 20-30 seconds (about 55-75 words at a warm pace).
frameworks.job: open on a proof stack that shows what you replaced, then stop the viewer on the fix they're thinking about, then ask for the click.
frameworks.awareness: problem aware, about to act on the wrong fix. The proof is the hook.
frameworks.proof: heavy. This is the one card where the proof is the opening line. With thin proof, use 04 or 06.

rows: What you replaced, how many, what it produced, what it costs. Every clause a number

"Last year, I replaced 26 B2B sales reps in 12 AI and digital service companies and generated 135 million in qualified sales pipeline using a revenue growth engine that requires just 7.4k a month to operate."
A specific thing they're thinking about right now, with a year
"So if you're still thinking about hiring more salespeople for your business to grow in 2026, stop."
One sentence on what you'll show them
"I'll show you how you can add 1 to 3 million in new revenue to your business in the next 12 months."
Five words and the qualify gate
"Click this ad and see if you qualify."

frameworks.title: Single-objection retargeting
frameworks.job: tell a warm viewer you know they're undecided, name the one objection holding them back, answer it with what people who went ahead got, and give a date.
frameworks.awareness: most aware. They've seen the offer and haven't acted. Warm traffic only.
frameworks.proof: one result with a timeframe, plus a volume number if you have one.

rows: Tells the viewer you know they've been looking and haven't decided
"We can see you're looking at the National Workplace Wellbeing Conference and you're still sitting on the fence."
**Name the objection, then the timeframed counter**
Says the exact objection in their words, then what people who went ahead got, inside a window
"If you're thinking two days out of the business is too much... leaders who invest in themselves for two days see reduced staff turnover, increased team performance and less burnout within 90 days."
Reframes the cost as a saving against a bigger cost later
"Two days of self development now will reduce time and money spent on fixing problems months later."
Social proof and a deadline in one line
"Join us and 300 other professionals on the 16th and 17th of September in Brisbane."
"Click the link below to secure your seat for the National Workplace Wellbeing Conference."

frameworks.title: Diagnostic pause
frameworks.job: ask a question the viewer can't answer, name the silence, explain why the whole category fails them, then redefine what you offer as a different kind of thing.
frameworks.awareness: unaware to problem aware. They've tried the category before and it didn't stick.
frameworks.proof: light. The viewer's own memory does the persuading. The redefinition has to be true of what you actually deliver.

rows: Ask them to name one lasting effect of the last comparable thing they did. The silence is the point, not the answer
"That pause you just felt is the whole problem."
Information alone doesn't compound. "You fly home fired up, and by Thursday you're back to the old playbook." A mechanism, not a claim
"You already know the right things to do. That was never the gap." Then one specific moment that names the real gap
"This is not a [old category]. It's a [new category]."
One sentence, as short as it will go. "You don't leave with information. You leave different."
Where and when, how many places, one action

frameworks.title: Why now, then what leaders do
frameworks.length: 45-60 seconds (about 120-160 words at a warm pace).
frameworks.job: name the real problem or the thankless reality, show why a new trend has made it worse right now, then show what leaders in the same seat are doing about it, and ask for a call.
frameworks.awareness: problem aware and feeling a new pressure they can't absorb with the same budget and team.
frameworks.proof: light. Peer behaviour does the persuading ("the leaders we work with are using...", or two recognisable company names). The full offer, guarantee and proof stack sit in the primary text, not the video.

rows: Either names the real problem behind the one they blame, or names what they deliver that nobody notices

"The problem isn't there are bugs. Honestly, there's always bugs. The problem is how do you find the gaps between all the different parts of the system?" / "You deliver consistently every month... But no one remembers that. They remember the three bugs that got through into production."
A current trend that has made the old problem worse this year, said as a fact the viewer already sees
"Developers, as we know, are generating 10x more code than ever before using AI tools."
Questions they can't answer, or the constraint they're stuck inside
"How do you keep up with that? How do you ensure that the data is clean, that all the different tools link together?" / "You only have the same budget you had last year, the same number of testers."
Peers in the same seat are already using a new kind of tool. Names the category and what it does, not the product

"Many of the industry leaders that we work with, they're using new tools and new techniques that have traceability and auditability." / "Companies like HPE and Generali, they're using modern agentic testing tools."
What changes for them, ending on what it means for the viewer personally
"That way they can have confidence in their release." / "And you can too. And that way the blame doesn't land at your desk."
Low-pressure next step, says who calls and for how long
"Click on the link and fill in the form and one of my team members will be happy to schedule a 30 minute call with you."
